paragraphs: The mitzvah of tefillin is very severe, and one who does not put on tefillin because the mitzvah is not important in his eyes is called one of the "transgressors of Israel in body," about whom it is stated in the Talmud a harsh and very bitter statement. Rav Sheshet further said: anyone who does not put on tefillin transgresses eight positive commandments. They are a sign for Israel, and a person must have proper intention when putting them on, that the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded us regarding these four passages, which contain the unification of His Name and the exodus from Egypt, to place them on the arm opposite the heart and on the head opposite the brain, so that we remember the miracles and wonders He performed with us, which testify to His unity and that He has the power and dominion over the upper and lower worlds to do with them as He wills, and so as to subjugate to the Holy One, blessed be He, the soul that is in the brain, and also the heart, which is the source of desires and thoughts — and thereby one remembers the Creator and lessens his pleasures.

clarification.explanation: The mitzvah of tefillin is very severe. One who does not put on tefillin because the mitzvah is not important in his eyes is considered among the "transgressors of Israel in body," about whom a harsh statement is made in the Talmud, and our Sages said that anyone who does not put on tefillin transgresses eight positive commandments. Tefillin are a sign for Israel, and a person must have intention when putting them on that the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded these four passages, which contain the unification of His Name and the exodus from Egypt, to be placed on the arm opposite the heart and on the head opposite the brain, so that we remember the miracles and wonders that testify to His unity and His dominion over the upper and lower worlds, and so that we subjugate to Him the soul that is in the brain and the heart, which is the source of desires and thoughts, and thereby remember the Creator and lessen [our] pleasures.
takeaways: Tefillin is a severe mitzvah; one who treats it lightly is counted among the "transgressors of Israel in body"
The intention: to subjugate the brain and the heart to the Creator and to remember His wonders and His unity

paragraphs: After putting on the tallit, one should put on tefillin immediately, before the passage of the Akedah, so that they are on him during the recitation of the Shema of the sacrificial offerings, which is obligatory. Our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said: anyone who recites the Shema without tefillin is as if he testifies false testimony about himself.

clarification.explanation: After a person has put on the tallit, he should put on tefillin immediately, before the recitation of the passage of the Akedah, so that they are on him during the recitation of the Shema that is part of the sacrificial portions, which is obligatory. And our Sages said that anyone who recites the Shema without tefillin is as if he testifies false testimony about himself.
takeaways: Tefillin are put on immediately after the tallit, before the passage of the Akedah
The purpose: to recite the Shema while wearing tefillin

paragraphs: According to the order of the higher aspects to which the tzitzit and tefillin allude, one must put on the tzitzit before the tefillin, and one who puts on tefillin first is in error, and of him it is said, "he who studied last is behind the schoolchildren." The halachic authorities made a mnemonic for this order: "vehayu ha'atufim leLavan vehakshurim leYa'akov" [the wrapped ones belonged to Lavan and the bound ones to Ya'akov]. They further said: the final letter of the word "tzitzit" is a tav, which is the first letter of the word "tefillin," and therefore "tzitzit" is an acronym for "Tzivah Hashem Tzitzit Yanichu Techilah" [the Lord commanded that tzitzit be put on first]. And in my holy book "Rav Pe'alim" I wrote in a responsum that if one was wearing tefillin without a tallit gadol — because he did not have one — and afterward they brought him the tallit, he must remove the tefillin, put on the tzitzit, and put the tefillin back on afterward, without a berachah.

clarification.explanation: According to the order of the higher aspects to which the tzitzit and tefillin allude, one must put on tzitzit before tefillin, and one who puts on tefillin first is in error. The halachic authorities gave a mnemonic for this: "vehayu ha'atufim leLavan vehakshurim leYa'akov." A further mnemonic: the letter tav at the end of the word "tzitzit" is also the first letter of the word "tefillin," teaching that tzitzit precedes tefillin; and likewise "tzitzit" is an acronym for "Tzivah Hashem Tzitzit Yanichu Techilah." And if a person was wearing tefillin without a tallit gadol (because he did not have one), and afterward they brought him a tallit, he must remove the tefillin, put on the tzitzit, and then put the tefillin back on again without a berachah.
takeaways: Tzitzit is put on before tefillin; one who puts on tefillin first is in error

Mnemonics for this: "vehayu ha'atufim leLavan vehakshurim leYa'akov"; the final letter (tav) of "tzitzit" is the first letter of "tefillin"; "tzitzit" is an acronym for "Tzivah Hashem Tzitzit Yanichu Techilah"
If the tallit arrives after he has already put on tefillin: he removes them, wraps himself [in the tallit], and puts them on again without a berachah

paragraphs: One who places the tallit and the tefillin bag inside a single bag should be careful to place the tefillin bag to the side of the tallit; for if he places it above the tallit, he will end up encountering the tefillin first, before the tallit; and if he places it below the tallit, that is disrespectful to the tefillin, whose sanctity is greater than that of the tallit — for even though it is inside the bag and not visible, one must still take care not to place it beneath the tallit. Therefore he should place it to the side, so that he will not encounter it first. And if it happens that he encounters the tefillin first, this does not obligate him to put on the tefillin before wrapping himself in the tzitzit; rather, even in such a case, where he encountered the tefillin first, he should be careful to put on the tallit before the tefillin.

clarification.explanation: One who places the tallit and the tefillin bag in one bag should be careful to place the tefillin bag to the side of the tallit. For if he places it above the tallit he will encounter the tefillin first, before the tallit (and would have to put them on first), and if he places it below the tallit, that is not respectful to the tefillin, whose sanctity is greater. Therefore he should place it to the side, so that he does not encounter it first. And even if he does encounter the tefillin first, this does not require him to put them on before the tallit — rather, he should still put the tallit on first.
takeaways: Place the tefillin bag beside the tallit, not above or below it
Even if one encounters the tefillin first, he still puts on the tallit before the tefillin

paragraphs: The holy Zohar greatly praised the one who leaves his house wrapped in tzitzit and crowned with tefillin and goes to the synagogue, reciting at the entrance the verse "Va'ani berov chasdecha..." ["But as for me, in the abundance of Your lovingkindness..."], and this mitzvah takes precedence even over the mitzvah of being among the first ten [in the synagogue], as written in Sha'ar HaKavanot of our teacher the Ari, of blessed memory. In a town where gentile passersby are commonly found in the streets and it is difficult to do this openly, some wise people find a way to wear a thin tallit and very small tefillin so that they are covered by a hat and unnoticed by onlookers, letting the tallit down over their shoulders and wearing a cloak over it; and upon arriving at the synagogue they remove the small tefillin mentioned and put on the tefillin of Rashi and Rabbeinu Tam that they keep there, and pray in them. I saw that the Rav "Chayei Adam," Klal 13, letter yud, suggested another way in this matter — that one put on the large tefillin at home and recite the berachah, etc., examine there. And in my holy books "Rav Pe'alim" I wrote, with Heaven's help, a responsum questioning his words on this, and in the end I concluded there that one should put on, at home, tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam made small, and in any case one does not recite a berachah over these tefillin, since one does not recite a berachah over the tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam, as we will explain further on. And I wrote there that one should not raise a question on this from what our teacher, of blessed memory, wrote in Sha'ar HaKavanot, that one must put on the Rashi tefillin before those of Rabbeinu Tam, because the supernal lights of the Rashi tefillin must first enter, and afterward those of Rabbeinu Tam — for one can say that our teacher, of blessed memory, was only strict about this where a person comes to put them on for the essential mitzvah, during the recitation of the Shema and the prayer — in which case he must put on the Rashi tefillin first; and furthermore he was speaking of a case where one comes to put both on together, where the Rashi tefillin also lie before him — in which case he must put on the Rashi tefillin first. This is not the case here, where he wears the Rabbeinu Tam tefillin alone, and moreover he does not put them on for the essential mitzvah but only in order to enter at the entrance of the synagogue and say the verse "Va'ani, etc." — in this there is no difficulty. And as I wrote there in the responsum, with Heaven's help, we wrote that after he enters the synagogue he should remove the Rabbeinu Tam tefillin and put on, there, the essential Rashi and Rabbeinu Tam tefillin that he has there, in their proper order, and recite the berachah over them, and this is more correct.

clarification.explanation: The Zohar greatly praised one who leaves his house wrapped in tallit and tefillin and recites "Va'ani berov chasdecha" at the entrance [of the synagogue], and this mitzvah even precedes the mitzvah of being among the first ten. Where gentile passersby are present and it is difficult to go out this way openly, some find a way to wear at home a thin tallit and small, hidden tefillin under a hat, and upon arriving at the synagogue remove them and put on the ordinary tefillin of Rashi and Rabbeinu Tam and pray in them. The Rav "Chayei Adam" suggested another way: to put on the ordinary large tefillin already at home and recite the berachah over them there, but our teacher [the author] questioned this in his book "Rav Pe'alim," and concluded that one should put on at home small tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam (over which one does not recite a berachah in any case), and there is no flaw in the order, since the requirement to put on Rashi's first applies only when putting them on for the essential mitzvah during the Shema and the prayer, or when both pairs are before him; here, however, he wears Rabbeinu Tam's alone, and only in order to enter the synagogue's entrance and recite "Va'ani." And when he enters the synagogue he should remove them and put on the essential Rashi and Rabbeinu Tam tefillin in their proper order and recite the berachah, and this is more correct.
takeaways: It is meritorious to leave one's house wrapped in tallit and tefillin and to recite "Va'ani berov chasdecha" at the entrance
The Rav "Chayei Adam" proposed putting on and reciting the berachah over the large tefillin already at home, but our teacher rejected this
Where gentiles are present: one should put on small Rabbeinu Tam tefillin at home (without a berachah) and exchange them at the synagogue

paragraphs: Through the wrapping of the tallit, the external aspect of the World of Yetzirah is rectified, and through the berachah of the tallit an encompassing light of the World of Yetzirah is made; through the tefillin of the arm the World of Beriah is rectified, and through the berachah an encompassing light of the World of Beriah is made; and through the tefillin of the head the World of Atzilut is rectified. Now, regarding the tefillin of the head, some say that one must recite a separate berachah in order to make the encompassing light of the World of Atzilut, and some say that it is not in our power to make this encompassing light of the World of Atzilut, but rather it comes about of itself, and therefore they hold that one should not recite a berachah over the tefillin of the head. The Ashkenazim recite a berachah over the tefillin of the head, following the opinion of the Geonim, while we, the children of the Sephardim, recite one berachah specifically over the tefillin of the arm, following the opinion of the Rif, of blessed memory; but we intend by this berachah also the tefillin of the head, which lies before us at the time of the berachah over the tefillin of the arm. However, if he interrupted between the tefillin of the arm and the tefillin of the head with something considered an interruption, then he should recite over the tefillin of the head, "asher kideshanu bemitzvotav vetzivanu al mitzvat tefillin." And likewise, if a person has only tefillin of the head and not of the arm, he recites over it "al mitzvat tefillin." And it is known that Heaven answered our teacher Rabbeinu Ya'akov of Troyes, of blessed memory, [through the verse] "ve'et beriti akim et Yitzchak" — this being [an allusion to] the Rif, of blessed memory; and also that we do not find that our teacher the Ari, of blessed memory, explicitly decided between the aforementioned opinions of the Rif and the Geonim, of blessed memory, but only mentioned the two opinions and explained their reasoning. However, in the books "Peri Etz Chayim" and also "Olat Tamid" we find his words stated simply as one berachah, and from the flow of his language it appears that he leans after the opinion of the Sephardim, to recite one berachah.

clarification.explanation: According to the secret [Kabbalah]: wrapping in the tallit rectifies the external aspect of the World of Yetzirah, and its berachah makes the encompassing light of that world; the tefillin of the arm rectify the World of Beriah and their berachah makes its encompassing light; and the tefillin of the head rectify the World of Atzilut. Regarding the tefillin of the head there is a dispute: some say one must recite a separate berachah over it to make the encompassing light of Atzilut, and some say it is not in our power to make this encompassing light — it comes about of itself — and therefore one should not recite a berachah over it. The Ashkenazim recite a berachah over the tefillin of the head, following the Geonim; we, the Sephardim, recite one berachah only over the tefillin of the arm, following the Rif, but intend by it also the tefillin of the head before us. If he interrupted between the arm and the head [tefillin] with a significant interruption, he recites over the head "al mitzvat tefillin"; likewise if he has only tefillin of the head, he recites over it "al mitzvat tefillin." It is further known that Heaven confirmed to our teacher Rabbeinu Ya'akov of Troyes (the author of the Tosafot), by allusion from the verse "ve'et beriti akim et Yitzchak," that his intention pointed to the Rif — a confirmation from Heaven for his opinion; and from the language of the Ari, of blessed memory, in his books "Peri Etz Chayim" and "Olat Tamid," it appears that he too leans toward reciting one berachah, following the opinion of the Sephardim, although he did not explicitly decide so.
takeaways: The Sephardim recite one berachah over the tefillin of the arm, and intend by it also the tefillin of the head
If one interrupted, or has only the tefillin of the head, he recites "al mitzvat tefillin"

It is told that Heaven confirmed to Rabbeinu Ya'akov of Troyes (by allusion from the verse "ve'et beriti akim et Yitzchak") the opinion of the Rif; and the Ari, too, leans toward reciting one berachah

paragraphs: It is forbidden to interrupt with speech between the tefillin of the arm and the tefillin of the head. Therefore, for us, the children of the Sephardim, who follow the opinion that one should not recite a separate berachah over the tefillin of the head — if one erred and came to recite a berachah over the tefillin of the head, and once he began saying "Baruch atah Hashem" he remembered [his error], he should not conclude "lamedeni chukecha," so that it should appear as though he is reciting a verse; for if he did so, it would constitute an interruption in speech between the tefillin of the arm and the tefillin of the head. Rather, he should conclude the berachah "al mitzvat tefillin," following the opinion that one does recite a berachah over the tefillin of the head by itself, as I concluded in my holy book "Makabtzi'el."

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to interrupt with speech between the tefillin of the arm and of the head. Therefore, for us, the Sephardim, who hold that one does not recite a separate berachah over the tefillin of the head, if one erred and began to recite a berachah over the tefillin of the head, and having started "Baruch atah Hashem" he remembered [his error], he should not conclude "lamedeni chukecha" (as though reciting a verse), since that would constitute a forbidden interruption between the tefillin of the arm and the head; rather, he should conclude the berachah "al mitzvat tefillin," following the opinion that one does recite a berachah over the tefillin of the head by itself.
takeaways: If one erred and opened a berachah over the tefillin of the head, he should conclude "al mitzvat tefillin," not "lamedeni chukecha"
The reason: reciting a verse would be considered a forbidden interruption between the tefillin of the arm and of the head

paragraphs: Most of the plain-sense halachic authorities hold that one should recite the berachah over the tefillin of the arm while standing, and a minority hold [it should be recited] while seated; the Kabbalists, of blessed memory, hold that one should recite the berachah while seated. In the writings of our teacher the Ari, of blessed memory, there is no clear statement found on this matter, and we here, in our town of Baghdad, are accustomed to recite the berachah while seated, following the opinion of the Kabbalists, of blessed memory, and so is the essential [practice].

clarification.explanation: Most of the plain-sense halachic authorities hold that the berachah over the tefillin of the arm is recited standing, and a minority hold seated; the Kabbalists hold that it is recited seated. There is no explicit ruling on this in the writings of the Ari, and in Baghdad the practice is to recite the berachah seated, following the opinion of the Kabbalists, and so is the essential [practice].
takeaways: There is a dispute whether the berachah over the tefillin of the arm is recited standing or seated
The berachah is recited seated, following the opinion of the Kabbalists, and so is the essential [practice]

paragraphs: One recites the berachah "lehani'ach" with a kamatz under the letter hei, from the language of "placing a berachah [to rest]," meaning that the tefillah rests and is settled in the place of the knot so that it does not sway back and forth, as Rav Moshe Zacuto, of blessed memory, wrote, and his words were cited in "Machazik Berachah," siman 25, examine there. And the berachah is recited after he has placed the tefillin of the arm on the kibboret, and immediately after the berachah he performs the tying and the tightening, since the tying is the beginning of the mitzvah; and he should not recite the berachah before placing it on the kibboret.

clarification.explanation: One recites the berachah "lehani'ach" with a kamatz under the hei, from the language of placing [to rest] a berachah — meaning the tefillah rests and is settled in the place of the knot and does not sway. The berachah is recited after placing the tefillin box of the arm on the "kibboret" (the muscle of the arm), and immediately after the berachah he ties and tightens it, since the tying is the beginning of the mitzvah; he should not recite the berachah before placing it on the kibboret.
takeaways: Pronunciation: "lehani'ach" with a kamatz under the hei
The berachah is recited after placing the box on the kibboret, and immediately afterward he ties and tightens it

paragraphs: It is forbidden to interrupt with speech between the tefillin of the arm and the tefillin of the head, and if one did interrupt, the berachah he recited over the tefillin of the arm does not cover the tefillin of the head, and he must then recite over the tefillin of the head "asher kideshanu bemitzvotav al mitzvat tefillin." This applies when he interrupted with extraneous matters not needed for putting on the tefillin; but if he interrupted with matters relevant to putting on the tefillin, he need not recite the berachah again over the tefillin of the head. Nevertheless, one should be careful from the outset not to interrupt at all — even hinting and winking with his eyes, or gesturing with his fingers, is forbidden between the tefillin of the arm and the tefillin of the head. And even if he hears Kaddish, Barchu, or Kedushah, he should not interrupt to answer, but should remain silent, listen, and direct his intention to what the congregation is saying; and if he forgot and did answer, even so he should not recite the berachah [again] over the tefillin of the head.

clarification.explanation: One may not interrupt with speech between the arm and the head [tefillin]; if he did, the berachah recited over the arm does not cover the head, and he must recite over the head "asher kideshanu bemitzvotav al mitzvat tefillin." This is when he interrupted with extraneous matters; but if he interrupted with matters relevant to putting on the tefillin, he need not recite the berachah again. Nevertheless, one should be careful from the outset not to interrupt at all, not even by hinting with the eyes or the fingers. Even upon hearing Kaddish, Barchu, or Kedushah, he should not interrupt to answer, but should remain silent, listen, and direct his intention; and if he forgot and answered, he still should not recite the berachah [again] over the head.
takeaways: If one interrupted with extraneous speech between the tefillin of the arm and the head: he recites over the head "al mitzvat tefillin"
One should not even answer Kaddish or Kedushah between the tefillin of the arm and the head, only listen and direct his intention

paragraphs: The time for putting them on in the morning is from when one can recognize a friend with whom he has some familiarity at a distance of four amot. It is better to delay than to put them on early; and if one erred and put on tefillin while it was still night and recited the berachah over them, he need not recite the berachah again once daylight comes, as stated by the later authorities, of blessed memory.

clarification.explanation: The time for putting on tefillin in the morning is from when one can recognize a friend with whom he is somewhat familiar at a distance of four amot. It is better to delay a bit rather than put them on early. And if one erred and put on tefillin while it was still night and recited the berachah over them, he need not recite the berachah again once it becomes light.
takeaways: The time for putting on [tefillin]: from when one can recognize a friend at a distance of four amot; it is preferable to delay
If one put them on and recited the berachah while it was still night: he does not repeat the berachah when it becomes light

paragraphs: On Shabbat and Yom Tov it is forbidden to put on tefillin, because these days are themselves a "sign," and if one puts on another sign during them, he ends up demeaning them. Also on Chol HaMoed it is forbidden for us, the children of the Sephardim, to put them on, because we hold that the days of Chol HaMoed, too, are a "sign"; but the Ashkenazim's custom is to put them on during Chol HaMoed.

clarification.explanation: On Shabbat and Yom Tov it is forbidden to put on tefillin, because these days are themselves a "sign," and one who puts on another sign during them demeans them. And also on Chol HaMoed it is forbidden for us, the Sephardim, to put them on, since they too are a "sign." But the Ashkenazim are accustomed to put them on during Chol HaMoed.
takeaways: Tefillin are not worn on Shabbat and Yom Tov, since these days are themselves a "sign"
The Sephardim also do not wear them on Chol HaMoed; the Ashkenazim do wear them

paragraphs: One who removed his tefillin with the intention of putting them back on immediately need not recite the berachah again. But if he removed them in order to enter the bathroom, even if his intention is to put them on again immediately, he must recite the berachah again, since it is forbidden to enter the bathroom wearing them. There are those who disagree about this, and since [the rule is that] a doubtful berachah is treated leniently, here too, he should not recite a full berachah, but should recite it without [mentioning] the Name and Sovereignty, and think the Name and Sovereignty in his mind. And if the tefillin slipped from their place unintentionally and he adjusts them to put them back in their place, he should not recite a berachah.

clarification.explanation: One who removed his tefillin with the intention of putting them back on immediately need not recite the berachah again. But if he removed them in order to enter the bathroom, even with the intention of putting them on again immediately, he must recite the berachah again, since it is forbidden to enter the bathroom wearing them. There are those who disagree, and since it is a doubt regarding berachot (which is treated leniently), he should not recite it with [mention of] the Name and Sovereignty, but recite it without them and think the Name and Sovereignty in his mind. And if the tefillin slipped from their place unintentionally and he adjusts them to return them, he should not recite a berachah.
takeaways: Removed with the intention of putting them right back on: no new berachah; removed to enter the bathroom: recites the berachah again (without the Name and Sovereignty, out of doubt)
Slipped unintentionally and he readjusted them: he does not recite a berachah

paragraphs: It is permitted to recite a berachah over borrowed tefillin, since a person fulfills his obligation with the tefillin of his fellow; but it is forbidden to recite a berachah over stolen tefillin, since that is a mitzvah performed through a transgression, and of this it is said, "and he who profits by robbery, blasphemes the Lord" (Tehillim 10:3). Therefore, one should not wear his fellow's tefillin without the owner's knowledge, since one who borrows without the owner's knowledge is [legally] a robber. In a time of pressing need, when it is not possible for him to wear them with the owner's knowledge because [the owner] is not present, and if he waits the time [for the mitzvah] will pass, he may then rely on the generosity of the people of Israel, who are pleased to have a mitzvah performed with their property; and it is good that afterward he inform the owner and ask his consent for what he did retroactively, if he is able to find him.

clarification.explanation: It is permitted to recite a berachah over borrowed tefillin, since one fulfills his obligation with his fellow's tefillin. But it is forbidden to recite a berachah over stolen tefillin, since that is a mitzvah performed through a transgression. Therefore one should not wear his fellow's tefillin without the owner's knowledge, since one who borrows without the owner's knowledge is [legally] a robber. In a case of pressing need, where it is not possible to obtain the owner's knowledge and the time [for the mitzvah] would otherwise pass, one may rely on the fact that it is pleasing to Israel to have a mitzvah performed with their property, and it is good that afterward he inform the owner and seek his consent retroactively.
takeaways: One may recite a berachah over borrowed tefillin with permission, but not over stolen ones
In a case of pressing need, one may rely on the owner's presumed goodwill, and inform him afterward

paragraphs: The order for putting on tefillin: first, one ties the tefillin of the arm on the left arm, on the "kibboret," which is the raised, swollen place of flesh called the kibboret, and he should cover his arm with the tallit so that the placing of the tefillin of the arm is done discreetly — there is a secret in this matter, and therefore even one sitting alone, and even in a dark room, should likewise cover the arm with the tallit; a support for this is the verse "ki yad al kes" (Shemot 17:15). And the Maharí Kashtro, of blessed memory, gave the reason from "vehayah lecha le'ot al yadecha" (Shemot 13:9) — "a sign for you," and not for others. And he should not make a wrap on the kibboret itself; rather, after tightening it well, he ties the yud [-shaped knot] with the strap together with the tefillin box — even though, in any case, the yud is already tied with a sinew thread to the box, since one may never separate the base of the box, as mentioned in the Zohar, Pinchas, page 136 — nevertheless there is a secret reason to tie the yud with the strap as well, in order to draw down to the yud three hundred seventy lights, corresponding to the numerical value of "retzuah" [strap], which is 370 including the kolel. As for what Rav "Shalmei Tzibbur," of blessed memory, wrote on page 40, halachah 11, I already cited his words in my holy book "Makabtzi'el" and raised a question on them there, examine there. And after tying the yud, he draws the strap to the arm and winds it around the arm in seven complete wraps; and the initial drawing of the strap at the start of the arm, on one side of the arm, is not counted as a wrap and is not included among the wraps — unlike what "Shem Chadash" wrote on page 126; therefore he should wind exactly seven complete wraps. And after winding the seven wraps, he should stand and put on the tefillin of the head while standing, since one should only put on the tefillin of the head after the seven wraps.

clarification.explanation: The order for putting on tefillin of the arm: he ties it on the "kibboret" (the raised muscle of the left arm) and covers the arm with the tallit, so that the placing is done discreetly — there is a secret in this; therefore even one sitting alone, and even in a dark room, covers the arm. There is no wrap made on the kibboret itself; rather, after tightening it well, he ties the yud [-knot] of the strap together with the box (there is a secret in this, to draw down to the yud three hundred seventy lights, corresponding to the numerical value of "retzuah"). Afterward he draws the strap and winds it around the arm in seven complete wraps (the first wrap at the start of the arm is not counted). And only after the seven wraps does he stand and put on the tefillin of the head, while standing.
takeaways: One ties the tefillin of the arm on the kibboret and covers the arm with the tallit (discreetly — there is a secret in this)
He winds seven complete wraps, and only afterward puts on the tefillin of the head, while standing

paragraphs: After putting on the tefillin of the head, he immediately finishes putting on the tefillin of the arm with three wraps that he winds on the middle finger, called the "amah": one wrap on the middle joint of the finger and two wraps on the lower joint. And according to the words of Rav "Matzat Shimurim," of blessed memory, one should recite, while making these wraps, the verse "Ve'erastich li le'olam, ve'erastich li betzedek uvemishpat uvechesed uverachamim, ve'erastich li be'emunah veyada'at et Hashem" (Hoshea 2:21–22).

clarification.explanation: After putting on the tefillin of the head, one immediately finishes the tefillin of the arm with three wraps on the middle finger (called the "amah"): one wrap on the middle joint and two wraps on the lower joint. According to "Matzat Shimurim," one recites during these wraps the verses "Ve'erastich li le'olam, ve'erastich li betzedek uvemishpat uvechesed uverachamim, ve'erastich li be'emunah veyada'at et Hashem."
takeaways: After the head [tefillin], one finishes the arm [tefillin] with three wraps on the middle finger
Custom is to recite the verses "Ve'erastich li" during them

paragraphs: After making the three wraps mentioned on the finger and finishing the tefillin of the arm, he tucks the straps of the tefillin of the head into his belt, in this order: the left strap he tucks into the upper end of the belt, opposite his chest, and the right strap he tucks into the lower end of the belt, so that it is opposite his navel, by the secret of "vehaachat gevohah mechavertah" ["and one was higher than the other," Daniel 8:3]. And it is known that Chesed is called "long" and Gevurah "short," as written in Petach Eliyahu: "one long and one short." All this is done so that they should not dangle down to the ground, as mentioned in "Matzat Shimurim" and in "Mishnat Chasidim." And what I have written — that the tucking of the straps into the belt is done after the three wraps on the finger — appears so from the language of our teacher Rav Chaim Vital, of blessed memory, in "Olat Tamid," page 44, examine there; and it is likewise explicit in the book "Mishnat Chasidim," and so I concluded in my holy book "Makabtzi'el," even though this matter is not explicit in Sha'ar HaKavanot of our teacher the Ari, of blessed memory.

clarification.explanation: After the three wraps on the finger and finishing the tefillin of the arm, he tucks the straps of the head tefillin into his belt: the left strap at the upper end of the belt, opposite the chest, and the right strap at the lower end, opposite the navel, by the secret of "one was higher than the other" (Chesed being long and Gevurah short). All this is so that the straps do not dangle down to the ground. This order — tucking the straps into the belt after the three wraps on the finger — is stated in the words of Rav Chaim Vital and in "Mishnat Chasidim."
takeaways: The straps of the head tefillin are tucked into the belt: left [strap] above (opposite the chest), right [strap] below (opposite the navel)
This is so that the straps do not dangle down to the ground

paragraphs: Before putting the tefillin of the head on his head, he should look at the seven "zayins" found within the two "shins" [on the box], which contain deep, hidden secrets, as written in the holy Zohar, and this is cited in the words of the later authorities, of blessed memory. And know that although Maran, of blessed memory, wrote at the end of se'if 27 that "it is good to put on the tefillin of the head uncovered," the Kabbalists, of blessed memory, hold that one should cover it with the tallit, bringing the tallit down to the end of the forehead; their reasoning is according to the secret, and so is the essential [practice].

clarification.explanation: Before putting the head tefillin on his head, he looks at the seven "zayins" within the two "shins" on the box, which contain deep secrets, as brought in the Zohar. And know that although Maran wrote that it is good to put on the head tefillin uncovered, the Kabbalists hold that one should cover it with the tallit down to the end of the forehead, their reasoning being according to the secret, and so is the essential [practice].
takeaways: Before putting them on, one looks at the seven zayins within the shins on the head-tefillin box
The Kabbalists cover the head tefillin with the tallit down to the end of the forehead, and so is the essential [practice]

paragraphs: One should be careful not to take the tefillin of the head out of its bag until he has put on the tefillin of the arm and tied it in the place of the kibboret. If there is an attendant present who wishes to prepare the tefillin of the head for him and take it out of the bag before he has wound the seven wraps on the arm, there is no problem with this; he need only be careful not to take it out of the bag until he ties the tefillin of the arm in the place of the kibboret. There are honored people for whom the attendant prepares, in their place in the synagogue, the tzitzit and tefillin, taking them out of the bags before they arrive, and one must protest against this practice, that they should not do so.

clarification.explanation: One should be careful not to remove the head tefillin from its bag until the arm tefillin is put on and tied on the kibboret. If an attendant wishes to prepare the head tefillin and take it out before the seven wraps on the arm are wound, there is no problem, as long as he does not take it out of the bag before the arm tefillin is tied on the kibboret. There are honored people for whom the attendant takes out the tzitzit and tefillin from the bags in advance of their arrival, and one must protest against this practice.
takeaways: One does not take the head-tefillin out of its bag until the arm-tefillin is tied on the kibboret
Tefillin should not be prepared and taken out of their bags before their owner arrives

paragraphs: One who wore only the tefillin of the head, because he did not have the tefillin of the arm, and after putting on the tefillin of the head they brought him the tefillin of the arm — I concluded in a responsum, with Heaven's help, in my holy books "Rav Pe'alim," that he must remove the tefillin of the head from himself in order to put on the tefillin of the arm first, and afterward put on the tefillin of the head [again]. I further concluded there, with Heaven's help, that if one was wearing tefillin without a tallit gadol, because he did not have a tallit gadol, and afterward they brought him a tallit gadol, he must remove the tefillin, put on the tallit, and then put on the tefillin again without a berachah, for this is necessarily so according to the words of our teacher the Ari, of blessed memory.

clarification.explanation: One who wore only the head tefillin, because he did not have the arm tefillin, and afterward they brought him the arm tefillin, must remove the head tefillin in order to put on the arm tefillin first, and afterward put on the head tefillin again. Likewise, if one wore tefillin without a tallit gadol (since he did not have one) and afterward they brought him a tallit, he must remove the tefillin, put on the tallit, and then put the tefillin back on without a berachah, as is necessarily so according to the words of the Ari.
takeaways: If the arm-tefillin arrives after one has already put on only the head-tefillin: he removes it, puts on the arm-tefillin, then the head-tefillin again
If a tallit arrives after one has already put on tefillin: he removes them, wraps himself in the tallit, and puts the tefillin back on without a berachah

paragraphs: There are four passages in the tefillin: "Kadesh," "Vehayah ki yevi'acha," "Shema," "Vehayah im shamoa," and this is their order according to the opinion of Rashi, of blessed memory; but according to the opinion of Rabbeinu Tam, of blessed memory, their order is: "Kadesh," "Vehayah ki yevi'acha," "Vehayah im shamoa," "Shema." The custom follows the opinion of Rashi, of blessed memory. And the Levush, of blessed memory, wrote that once the platform over the grave of Yechezkel the Prophet, peace be upon him, collapsed, and they found there very old tefillin, which were in Rashi's order. Now, at first this dispute was thought to be like other disputes, where one opinion is rejected; but our teacher the Ari, of blessed memory, came and stated, by tradition from the mouth of Eliyahu, remembered for good, that both opinions are true, and one must fulfill both of them; and from the days of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, until the Geonim, people used to put on two pairs, and so it is stated in the Gemara: there is room on the head to put on two pairs. And in the Zohar Chadash it is stated regarding some people who put on two pairs out of doubt, "who do not know this secret, that both are needed." Therefore, one who fears Heaven should make two pairs of tefillin, one according to the opinion of Rashi and one according to the opinion of Rabbeinu Tam, and hold both in his hand and place them on his arm, tying one above the other, for he must put both on together, and not like those who put on Rashi's alone and Rabbeinu Tam's alone. He must also place the tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam above those of Rashi, both on the head and on the arm, because the level to which the tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam correspond is higher than the level of those of Rashi, and therefore the custom is to make the box of Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin smaller than that of Rashi's. The side attached to the arm is the upper one, so he should first put in Rashi's tefillin and recite the berachah over it after tying it on the kibboret, and afterward put in Rabbeinu Tam's, so that Rabbeinu Tam's ends up placed above Rashi's. All this concerns the boxes; but as for the straps, he should place the strap of Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin beneath the strap of Rashi's, and therefore he should make the width of Rabbeinu Tam's strap narrower than Rashi's, so that it is covered by it; and likewise for the head tefillin, he should place Rabbeinu Tam's above Rashi's, and also the knot of Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin should be at the back of the neck slightly higher than Rashi's; and only the straps descending from the knot at the back of the neck downward, he should pass Rabbeinu Tam's strap beneath Rashi's strap, so that it is covered by it — an allusion to this: "shemor tam ure'eh yashar" ["mark the perfect man and behold the upright"] (Tehillim 37:37). For all these matters there is a reason according to the secret, and one should not change them. He should also be careful not to place the box of one on top of the strap-loop of the other, but rather they should be adjacent, one beneath the other, all resting on the flesh, as I wrote, with Heaven's help, in my holy book "Makabtzi'el."

clarification.explanation: The four passages in the tefillin are "Kadesh," "Vehayah ki yevi'acha," "Shema," and "Vehayah im shamoa" — this is their order according to Rashi; but according to Rabbeinu Tam their order is "Kadesh," "Vehayah ki yevi'acha," "Vehayah im shamoa," "Shema." The custom follows Rashi (and the Levush wrote that very old tefillin found once at the grave of the Prophet Yechezkel were in Rashi's order). At first this dispute was thought to be like other disputes where one opinion is rejected, but the Ari, of blessed memory, stated by tradition from the mouth of Eliyahu that both opinions are true and one must fulfill both; and from the days of Moshe Rabbeinu until the Geonim, people wore two pairs (and the Gemara states: there is room on the head to put on two pairs). Therefore one who fears Heaven should make two pairs — one following Rashi and one following Rabbeinu Tam — and place them together on his arm, tying one above the other (not each pair separately). And the tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam are placed above those of Rashi (both on the head and the arm), since their level is higher (and therefore the custom is to make Rabbeinu Tam's box smaller than Rashi's). Since the side attached to the arm is the upper one, he puts in Rashi's first and recites the berachah over it after tying it on the kibboret, and then Rabbeinu Tam's (so that Rabbeinu Tam's ends up above). As for the straps, Rabbeinu Tam's strap passes beneath Rashi's strap (so its width is made narrower, to be covered); and likewise on the head, Rabbeinu Tam's is placed above, its knot at the back of the neck slightly higher, and its descending strap passes beneath Rashi's strap (alluded to in "shemor tam ure'eh yashar"). All this has a reason according to the secret and should not be changed; and one must be careful that the box of one is not placed on the strap-loop of the other, but that both rest adjacent, one beneath the other, on the flesh.
takeaways: The order of the passages: Rashi and Rabbeinu Tam disagreed; the Ari stated (from Eliyahu) that both opinions are true — therefore one who fears Heaven wears two pairs together

Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin are placed above Rashi's (on the head and the arm); one puts on Rashi's first and recites the berachah, then Rabbeinu Tam's; Rabbeinu Tam's strap passes beneath Rashi's strap ("shemor tam ure'eh yashar")
All this is according to the secret — not to be changed; and the boxes must be adjacent, one beneath the other, on the flesh (not one box on the other's strap-loop)

paragraphs: One should not recite a berachah over the tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam, even if one wears them alone, and the reason is that the level of the tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam is higher than that of Rashi's, according to the secret. And it is known that our teacher the Ari, of blessed memory, gave a reason for not reciting a berachah even over the tefillin of the head [of Rashi], because it is not in our power to draw down the light flowing from the level to which the tefillin of the head of Rashi correspond, and all the more so those of Rabbeinu Tam. And so wrote the Ramà, that one should not recite a berachah, and so was the practice of the elder rabbis of the Land of Israel. These are the words of Rav Moshe Zacuto, of blessed memory, which the Gaon Chida cited in "Machazik Berachah," siman 34, letter gimmel.

clarification.explanation: One does not recite a berachah over the tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam, even wearing them alone, because their level is higher than Rashi's according to the secret, and the Ari gave a reason for not reciting a berachah even over the head tefillin of Rashi — that it is not in our power to draw down the light of that level — all the more so with those of Rabbeinu Tam. So wrote the Ramà, and so was the practice of the elder sages of the Land of Israel, as cited by the Chida in the name of Rav Moshe Zacuto.
takeaways: One does not recite a berachah over the tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam, even when wearing it alone
The reason, according to the secret: we do not have the power to draw down the light of that level

paragraphs: Our teacher the Ari, of blessed memory, at first had the custom of wearing at Shacharit both the tefillin of Rashi and of Rabbeinu Tam, and at Minchah, those of Rabbeinu Tam alone. Afterward he made tefillin of Rashi according to the opinion of "Shimusha Rabba," which are two fingerbreadths by two fingerbreadths, and he would wear at Shacharit those of Rashi and Rabbeinu Tam, and at Minchah he would wear the aforementioned Shimusha Rabba tefillin, and he would say that these tefillin of Shimusha Rabba stand in place of the two opinions mentioned, and this is the reason they are two fingerbreadths, corresponding to the two aspects mentioned, all as explained in Sha'ar HaKavanot, examine there. And what he said, that they "stand in place of the two opinions," was for the time of the Minchah prayer, but not for the time of the Shacharit prayer, for if so, he would have worn them at Shacharit as well. Fortunate is the one who merits and is careful to pray Minchah in the Shimusha [Rabba] tefillin, the crown of heads; the teacher [Rav] my father, may his memory be for the life of the World to Come, was careful about this in the month of Elul and the Ten Days of Repentance. And know that those who are accustomed to pray Minchah in tefillin do not put them on for the Minchah of Erev Shabbat, because the holiness of Shabbat has already begun to sparkle, [Shabbat] itself being a "sign," as Rabbeinu Chida wrote in "Machazik Berachah," siman 25, in the name of the Kabbalist Maharam Papirash, of blessed memory, and "Shomer Emunim," examine there.

clarification.explanation: The Ari, of blessed memory, at first had the custom of wearing at Shacharit both Rashi's and Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin, and at Minchah those of Rabbeinu Tam alone. Afterward he made tefillin of Rashi according to "Shimusha Rabba" (two fingerbreadths by two fingerbreadths), and he wore these at Minchah, saying they stand in place of both opinions — which is why they are two fingerbreadths, corresponding to the two aspects. This was said only for the time of Minchah, not Shacharit (otherwise he would have worn them at Shacharit as well). Fortunate is one who merits praying Minchah in these tefillin; the author's father was careful about this in Elul and the Ten Days of Repentance. And those accustomed to pray Minchah in tefillin do not put them on for the Minchah of Erev Shabbat, since the holiness of Shabbat has already begun to sparkle, Shabbat itself being a "sign."
takeaways: It is meritorious to pray Minchah in tefillin (of "Shimusha Rabba," which stand in place of the two opinions)
Tefillin are not put on for the Minchah of Erev Shabbat, since the holiness of Shabbat has already begun to sparkle

paragraphs: One whose practice is to wear the tefillin of Rashi and of Rabbeinu Tam together, and erred and took Rabbeinu Tam's first, put it on and recited the berachah over it, and when he came to take the second one realized his error, that he had recited the berachah over Rabbeinu Tam's, should tie on Rashi's tefillin without a berachah, relying on the berachah he recited over Rabbeinu Tam's, since his practice every day is to wear both together, and his intention in the berachah was for both, since Rashi's tefillin was also lying before him at the time of the berachah, and his intention was to put it on — so wrote the responsa "Divrei Chaim," Yoreh De'ah, at the end of his responsum, siman 82, examine there, and this is correct. However, if his practice is to wear only Rashi's tefillin, and he took Rabbeinu Tam's by mistake, thinking it was Rashi's, and recited the berachah over it, and afterward it became known to him that he had taken Rabbeinu Tam's and recited the berachah over it, he must recite the berachah again when he puts on Rashi's. This situation occurs when a person borrows tefillin from his fellow, who has two pairs, Rashi's and Rabbeinu Tam's, and he wishes to wear only Rashi's, but by mistake took Rabbeinu Tam's and recited the berachah over it, and his fellow told him, and he wishes to put on Rashi's after that berachah.

clarification.explanation: One whose practice is to wear Rashi's and Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin together, who erred and took Rabbeinu Tam's first, put it on and recited the berachah, and when reaching for the second realized his error, should tie on Rashi's without a [new] berachah, relying on the one he recited, since his daily practice is to wear both together and his intention in the berachah was for both (Rashi's also being before him at the time). But one whose practice is Rashi's alone, who mistakenly took Rabbeinu Tam's thinking it was Rashi's and recited the berachah, and afterward learned of his mistake, must recite the berachah again when putting on Rashi's. This occurs, for example, when borrowing tefillin from a fellow who has both pairs.
takeaways: One accustomed to both pairs together, who mistakenly recited the berachah over Rabbeinu Tam's: ties on Rashi's without a [new] berachah
One accustomed to Rashi's alone, who mistakenly recited the berachah over Rabbeinu Tam's: must recite the berachah again over Rashi's

paragraphs: After putting on the tefillin, one should recite the passages of "Kadesh" and "Vehayah ki yevi'acha," in order to complete the four passages every day, as the Ramban and our teacher Rav Chaim Vital, of blessed memory, wrote. And if he is unable to recite them before the prayer, he should recite them after the prayer, as mentioned in "Machazik Berachah."

clarification.explanation: After putting on the tefillin, one recites the passages "Kadesh" and "Vehayah ki yevi'acha," in order to complete the recitation of the four passages every day ("Shema" and "Vehayah im shamoa" already being recited in the Shema). If he cannot recite them before the prayer, he recites them afterward.
takeaways: After putting on [tefillin], one recites "Kadesh" and "Vehayah ki yevi'acha" to complete the four passages
If he could not say them before the prayer, he says them afterward

paragraphs: After putting on the tefillin of the arm, before putting on the tefillin of the head, one should not interrupt even for Kaddish or Kedushah. In my responsum, with Heaven's help, in my holy books "Rav Pe'alim," I concluded, regarding one who wears the tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam alone, and it happens that Kaddish or Kedushah occurs between the tefillin of the arm and the head — even though in this case there is no berachah and no interruption [of a berachah] — nevertheless, according to the reasoning of the Ran and the "Levush," who hold that the reason one does not interrupt between the arm and the head is because it is written "vehayu" (Devarim 6:8), [implying] that there must be one single act for both of them; see "Minchat Aharon," page 37, who wrote a reason for this according to the secret; therefore one must be careful about this even with Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin, even though there is no berachah involved. However, I made a remedy for this, so as not to lose out on [answering] Kaddish and Kedushah: since there is no berachah here, he should answer the Kaddish and Kedushah, and after answering, he should remove the tefillin of the arm and put it back on anew, and after it the tefillin of the head, without interruption, thereby fulfilling what Scripture says, "vehayu" (Devarim 6:8), one single act for both of them; and this way, too, is correct according to the secret.

clarification.explanation: After putting on the arm tefillin and before the head tefillin, one should not interrupt even for Kaddish or Kedushah. Even one who wears Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin alone (where there is no berachah and thus, seemingly, no interruption of a berachah) must still be careful about this, according to the reasoning of the Ran and the "Levush," who explain the requirement of not interrupting from the verse "vehayu" — that both must form a single act. The remedy, so as not to lose out on Kaddish and Kedushah: since there is no berachah involved, he should answer the Kaddish and Kedushah, and afterward remove the arm tefillin and put it back on anew, followed immediately by the head tefillin without interruption, thereby fulfilling "vehayu" as a single act for both — and this way is also correct according to the secret.
takeaways: One does not interrupt for Kaddish or Kedushah between the arm and head tefillin, even when wearing Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin alone
With Rabbeinu Tam's alone: he answers, then removes the arm-tefillin and puts it back on together with the head-tefillin, without interruption
